references.text: The Lord encourages courage and strength, just as Gideon was promised that his hands would be strengthened after hearing what the enemy said.
The Lord gives the enemy into Israel's hand, paralleling the promise that Gideon's hands would be strengthened before attacking the Midianite camp.
Jonathan and his armor-bearer went down toward the Philistine camp, in a similar way as Gideon and his servant Pura went down to the edge of the enemy camp.
The Spirit of the Lord came upon Gideon and gave him courage, which is the background for why he needed further confirmation and strength in chapter 7.
The call to be strong and courageous is repeated throughout Scripture, just as Gideon was promised that his hands would be strengthened.
The prophet urges strengthening weak hands and encouraging fearful hearts, paralleling the promise to Gideon that his hands would become strong.
